title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a continuation (sheet '22') of §6 of the Teichmülleries notes. Grothendieck is finishing an explicit identification of the extended (orientation-reversing) orbifold fundamental group of a regular spherical tessellation X_n with an extended triangle group.

Setting. X_n is the sphere tiled with n-fold symmetry about the poles P_±. On the previous page he constructed
 g_n : π_1(X_n^*, D_n; P_{n+}) ≅ Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n⟩.
The target is the orbifold fundamental group of P^1_C with ramification ν_n = ∞·{0} + 2·{1} + n·{∞}, i.e. the (∞,2,n) triangle group. Generators map as ε_0 ↦ ρ_0, σ_{a0} ↦ ρ_1, ρ ↦ ρ_∞^{-1}.

He then extends this, as (99), to the version with complex conjugation:
 π_1(X_n^*, D_n×{1,τ}) ≅ (Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n⟩)·{1, τ̃}.
To finish he needs the image of one orientation-reversing element, σ̃_{a0}. Geometrically this is the reflection of X_n in a great circle through P_∞, Q_{a0}, P_{∞'}.

Computing g_n(σ̃_{a0}). On this page he pushes the path α̃_σ from P' = σ̃°_{a0}(P) to P forward by g_n. It becomes a path in the orbifold of P^1 from τ(P_+) = P_- to P_+. This path crosses the real 'equator' exactly once, on the arc (1,∞). The figure labels the real circle with arcs a_0 = (0,1), a_1 = (1,∞), a_∞ = (∞,0). So the image is the reflection τ_{a1}, written τ_0 because the arc a_1 is opposite the vertex 0. This gives (*): g_n(σ̃_{a0}) = τ_0 in Π^τ_{0,3}/⟨ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n⟩.

Consistency check. He compares with the action formulas (86), σ̃_{a0}(ρ) = ρ^{-1}, which must give τ_0(ρ_∞^{-1}) = ρ_∞ and τ_0(ρ_1) = ρ_1^{-1}. These are the standard facts that a mirror reflection inverts the rotations about vertices on that mirror. He cross-references the earlier n=3 case.

Second formula. Using τ_{a0} = σ̃_{a0}·σ_{a0} and the relation ρ_1 = τ_0 τ_∞ (rotation about vertex 1 = product of the reflections in the two sides through 1), he gets g_n(τ_{a0}) = τ_0 ρ_1 = τ_∞. Summary (100): g_n(σ̃_{a0}) = τ_0, g_n(τ_{a0}) = τ_∞.

Section 7 begins. He returns to maps ('cartes'). The group Π^τ_P, for P a weighted polygon, is to be read as a 'weighted polygonal cartographic group'. On the next page this becomes an equivalence between finite P-weighted maps and finite Π^τ_P-sets on which the involutions τ_a act without fixed points (the set acted on is the set of faces, i.e. chambers). The oriented version uses Π_P and the 'direct' faces. This generalizes the cartographic groups C_2 and C_2^+ of the Esquisse from triangles to arbitrary weighted polygons.

Purpose. The goal is an explicit combinatorial dictionary between regular tessellations and the (∞,2,n) / extended triangle orbifold groups. It fits Grothendieck's program of describing coverings of M_{0,n}-type orbifolds and the Teichmüller tower through maps and their real structure (complex conjugation).
errors: No mathematical error detected. The relations τ_0ρ_1 = τ_∞ (given τ_0^2 = 1 and ρ_1 = τ_0τ_∞) and τ_0(ρ_1) = ρ_1^{-1}, τ_0(ρ_∞^{-1}) = ρ_∞ are correct for an extended triangle group.

Notational overload, not an error: τ_{a0} denotes a reflection on the X_n side, while on the previous page τ_∞ := τ_{a0} on the X_0 side. Also the remark 'prenant ici pour a_0 le côté (1,∞)' relabels arcs relative to the figure, where a_0 = (0,1). This needs care when reading but is internally consistent.

ideas.what: Explicit isomorphism of the extended orbifold fundamental group of a regular spherical tessellation with the extended (∞,2,n) triangle group, including images of reflections
ideas.modern_name: Extended triangle (reflection) groups as orbifold fundamental groups / Belyi-type uniformization of regular maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Coxeter); maps via triangle groups: Jones–Singerman 1978
ideas.where_published: Only the general philosophy appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Computing the image of a reflection by counting crossings of the real locus by a path from τ(P_+) to P_+
ideas.modern_name: Real structure / complex conjugation on the orbifold fundamental group via real arcs (cf. 'tangential base points' and real points of M_{0,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; real-structure analyses by Huisman, Ihara and others

ideas.what: Weighted polygonal cartographic group Π^τ_P: finite P-weighted maps are equivalent to finite Π^τ_P-sets with fixed-point-free involutions τ_a (faces as chambers); oriented version with Π_P
ideas.modern_name: Chamber systems / maps as permutation representations of polygonal reflection (Coxeter-type orbifold) groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tits (chamber systems), Jones–Singerman, Vince (combinatorial maps); triangle case: Grothendieck's cartographic group in Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme treats only the triangle case (C_2, C_2^+); the polygonal weighted generalization is not known to me in his published texts

missed.claim: Grothendieck extends his cartographic-group dictionary from triangles (the Esquisse) to arbitrary weighted polygons P. He treats it inside the Teichmüller-tower/orbifold framework, including the τ (real/orientation-reversing) version.
missed.quote: le groupe π^τ_p s'interprète comme le groupe "cartographique pondéré polygonal"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The mathematics is essentially known (chamber systems, polygonal reflection groups). Its explicit placement by Grothendieck as the polygon analogue of C_2 is a small historical detail absent from accounts of the Esquisse's cartographic groups.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine bookkeeping of generator images in an extended triangle group. The start of §7 on 'weighted polygonal cartographic groups' is a modest unpublished generalization of the Esquisse notion, but the underlying mathematics (maps as permutation representations of reflection groups) is standard.
transcription_corrections: First line: likely 'Par g_n ce chemin devient un chemin dans U_{0,3}' rather than 'Pour que ce chemin devient...'.
'g_n(α̃_∞)' should be 'g_n(α̃_σ)', the path α̃_σ from the previous page.
'à (86)' is likely 'de (86)'; '... donnent[?] bien' is likely '... donnent bien'.

'ce qui est contenu en effet dans les § (dans un premier paragraphe)' is likely 'ce qui est contenu en effet dans les formules (86) pour n=3, en prenant ici pour a_0 le côté (1,∞) du triangle (0,1,∞) dans X_0'.
Margin figure: the sphere with the real circle labelled a_∞, ∞, a_1, 0, a_0, 1, i.e. arcs a_0 = (0,1), a_1 = (1,∞), a_∞ = (∞,0), next to the label (*).
'{+du §6+}' insertion: 'Dans toutes ces considérations du §6, on a un peu perdu de vue les cartes, dont il n'a plus été question.'
